'''Buz M. Walker''' (August 20, 1863 – August 21, 1949)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eVUSRNLQAmgC|title=SCHOOL AND SOCIETY|year=1949|publisher=}}</ref> was a [[mathematics]] professor and the President of the Mississippi Agricultural and Mechanical College (now [[Mississippi State University]]) from 1925 to 1930.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.msstate.edu/president/timeline/ |title=President's Office (Mississippi State University) |accessdate=2010-12-26 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101226172528/http://www.msstate.edu/president/timeline/ |archivedate=2010-12-26 }}</ref> The Walker Engineering building at Mississippi State is named in his honor.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.msstate.edu/web/maps/index.php?building=0075|title=Mississippi State University|publisher=}}</ref> He was an instructor at the school from 1883 to 1884, an assistant professor of mathematics from 1888 to 1927, dean of the engineering school from 1922 to 1925, and vice president of the university from 1913 to 1925.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.starkvilledailynews.com/content/days-pastthe-history-walker-building|title=From Days Past....The History of the Walker Building - Starkville Daily News|website=www.starkvilledailynews.com|access-date=2018-01-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180117012231/http://www.starkvilledailynews.com/content/days-pastthe-history-walker-building|archive-date=2018-01-17|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was also involved with the school's athletics, a regular member of the [[Southern Intercollegiate Athletic Association]], and its president around the time of [[World War I]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/16587465/the_atlanta_constitution/|author=Dick Jemison|author-link=Dick Jemison|page=3|work=The Atlanta Constitution|date=December 9, 1917|title=New Orleans Is Selected For 1918 S. I. A. A. Meet|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref>

He graduated from Mississippi A&M with the class of 1883. From 1885 to 1887 Walker attended the [[University of Virginia]] and studied under professor William M. Thornton.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rUwTAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA897|title=Mississippi: Contemporary biography|first=Dunbar|last=Rowland|date=16 January 2018|publisher=Reprint Company|via=Google Books|page=897|isbn=9780871522221}}</ref>

==Mathematics==
Buz M. Walker achieved worldwide distinction in 1906 with a [[University of Chicago]] dissertation "On the Resolution of the Higher Singularities of Algebraic Curves Into Ordinary Nodes", supervised by [[Oskar Bolza]].<ref name=Autobiography/> Walker was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 1936 in Oslo.<ref>{{cite book|author=Walker, B. M.|chapter=The higher singularities of algebraic curves|title=''In:'' Comptes rendus du Congrès international des mathématiciens: Oslo, 1936|volume=2|page=82|year=1937}}</ref><ref name=Autobiography>{{cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MUtLAAAAMAAJ&pg=PA53|title=On the Resolution of Higher Singularities of Algebraic Curves Into Ordinary ...|publisher=|last1=Walker|first1=Buz M.|year=1906}}</ref>
